chunks: When Moses had fulfilled the term and was journeying with his family, he noticed a fire on the side of the mountain. "Wait here," he said to his family; "I have seen a fire. I may haply bring some news from there, or an ember that you may warm yourselves."

key_terms.جَذْوَةٍ: an ember or stick of fire

ai.seo_question: What did Moses tell his family to do when he saw the fire on the side of the mountain?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this moment marks the transition from Moses' earthly preparation to his spiritual awakening, where the 'fire' (Nar) serves as a divine signpost leading to the burning bush. The Prophet's request for an 'ember' (Jadwa) is interpreted not merely for physical warmth but as a metaphor for acquiring spiritual light and knowledge before receiving the ultimate revelation. This event underscores the Shia emphasis on the necessity of divine guidance (Hujjah) preceding prophetic mission.
